checks: The interpolant has increasing slopes, and the base interval [0,9] supplies exactly the ten prescribed positive fibers.

Exact rational replay gives two strict complementary strip gaps, original cap masses 500 and 500, and maximum fiber fraction 257/2000. Each cap strictly owns a nonempty group, proving inclusion-minimality.
With the complementary interval below an original fiber, an in-fiber center must be the lower endpoint to avoid a finite-scale hit. With it above, the upper endpoint is required.

The four distinct quadratic endpoint values require two separate secants through two sites each. Exact evaluation of all secants on the six right sites gives at most 39<257/2, so neither secant can provide a right-side selector.

The exterior map p stays in the complementary strip and moves both sets of intervals away from it. For the normalized balance of the two opposite continuous normals, averaging the two right-hand sides gives complementary term 1/2.
Source 7e247486f83d7d21 §5, equation (9), has exactly these constants and distinguishes in-fiber and exterior centers.

overlap.comparison: The normalized continuous circuit criterion detects complementary-fiber emptiness. Here its constant positive term carries no information about the varying endpoint constraints for a dilation selector.

readability: The cap masses are the original closed masses. The preservation claim concerns the fixed open cover, with no asserted preservation of its numerical mass budget.
review_method: Independent frozen proof read, source and predecessor comparison, and exact rational replay where numerical claims occur.
summary: The exact ten-fiber polygon and both cap budgets check out, and the obstruction applies to arbitrary two-region partitions with genuine selectors.
